crime: Every evening, a girl walked the long path around the lake to draw the lights of the prison from the far shore, and {WITCH_NAME} ran straight across the water to sit with her.
One evening at seven, by the lake, the girl handed her the sketchbook full of those lights. "You keep it. I've drawn it enough."
{WITCH_NAME}'s mother had once given her things away one by one: her coat to a neighbour, her books to her daughter. Then one morning she was gone. People hand out what they own before they leave.

{WITCH_NAME} pulled the girl's scarf tight around her neck and held it until the girl went still. Then she used her Magic: carrying the girl, she ran across the lake and sat her down on the far shore, facing the prison lights, where she always drew. At ten past seven she came back into the lounge and stayed among the prisoners all evening.

They had all seen the girl leave the lounge for the long lake path at five to seven, and her spot was twenty minutes away on foot. So in the trial court, the prisoners ruled that she had walked out there and been strangled at her spot, by which time {WITCH_NAME} was already back among them.

Then a prisoner turned over the dead girl's shoes. Nobody walks the lake path through the forest without coming back with pine needles stuck to their soles. Hers were clean. The prisoners saw it then: she had never walked the path. {WITCH_NAME} had carried her across the water before ten past seven.
fields.epitaph: It was only a sketchbook. She outran a goodbye that was never coming.
fields.epithet: The Girl Who Runs Ahead of Every Goodbye
execution: In the trial court, the execution stand opens a deep, round pool skinned with thin lake ice and ringed with the prison lights. It sets her down in the middle of the ice and lets go. She breaks into a run.
The ice holds her only as long as she keeps moving. She runs toward a light, and it goes dark before she reaches it. Then the next, and the next, each one out before she gets there.
In the dark, she stumbles to a stop. The ice gives way, and she drops through.
The black water goes still in the broken ice. Nothing rises under the dark ring.

magic.name: Skipping Stone
magic.text: She can run across water, thin ice or a taut rope as if it were solid ground.
